newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsican police attacked, leaders quizzed.
newsitem.headline: Corsican police attacked, leaders quizzed.

text.p: Corsican gunmen attacked two more police stations on the French Mediterranean island on Tuesday as investigators probing a failed extortion bid questioned the main hardline separatist leader and his girlfriend in Paris.

In the latest of almost daily attacks, guerrillas hit a paramilitary gendarmerie barracks in the northern port of Calvi with a rocket-propelled grenade at 5.30 a.m. (0430 GMT), blowing a hole in the wall but causing no casualties.
Ten minutes later, assailants fired on a gendarmerie post in Vescovato, on the east coast of the island, with shotguns. No one was injured there either.

Meanwhile, police were questioning Francois Santoni, general secretary of Cuncolta Naziunalista, legal front for the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front-Historic Wing, and his girlfriend, Marie-Helene Mattei, the leading separatist lawyer.

Justice sources said the two would be brought before France's top anti-terrorism magistrate later on Tuesday to be formally placed under investigation in connection with an attempt to extort "revolutionary tax" from a Corsican golf club.
The owner refused to pay four million francs ($800,000) and, in a rare act of cooperation with the police in Corsica, called in detectives after the groundsman's house was blown up last Thursday.
He alleged that Mattei had told him on her cellphone to expect the "collectors."

Police arrested her on Monday morning as she tried to board a plane for Paris. Santoni, who had been living on the run since he was sentenced in his absence in October to four months in prison for carrying guns, turned himself in the same day.
Of eight suspects being held in the golf club bombing, five were expected to be charged on Tuesday.

Justice sources said star anti-terror magistrate Jean-Louis Bruguiere was expected to be put in charge of investigating the case, signalling the government's determination to crack down on the Corsican guerrillas.
